pages.title: Ride
pages.purpose: Road craft, technique and awareness for roads that do not forgive assumptions.
pages.lede: Most incidents on East African roads are not caused by speed alone. They are caused by a rider reading the road with expectations built somewhere else. This section covers what the road actually does.

pages.title: Navigate
pages.purpose: Routes, route notes, fuel planning and terrain preparation across the region.
pages.lede: A route is not a line on a map. It is a fuel plan, a surface report, a weather window and an honest estimate of how long the last sixty kilometres will actually take.

pages.title: Survive
pages.purpose: Breakdowns, first aid, weather and the preparation that happens before any of it.
pages.lede: The gap between an inconvenience and an emergency is usually preparation. This section is about the hour after something goes wrong, and the ten minutes before you left that decided how that hour goes.

pages.title: Maintain
pages.purpose: Maintenance guides, service intervals and diagnostics tuned for local conditions.
pages.lede: Service books are written for clean fuel, sealed roads and mild dust. Adjust the intervals or the bike will adjust them for you, usually at the least convenient point on the route.

plate.title: Naming the parts
plate.caption_right: Reference diagram, not a specific machine
plate.body: Half of a phone diagnosis is lost to vocabulary. If you can tell a fundi that the noise is at the swingarm pivot rather than somewhere at the back, you get a useful answer on the first call and you pay for one repair instead of two. The specification block on this drawing is marked as an example, because the numbers that matter are the ones in your own manual.

pages.title: Equip
pages.purpose: What riders should carry, use and choose. Equipment judged against heat, dust, load and price, tested where possible and marked honestly where not.
pages.lede: Everything here has either been used on a route or inspected in person. Where we have not tested something we say so, and where a price moves with the exchange rate we say that too.

plate.title: Condition, not packaging
plate.body: A helmet is the one item on this page where used is the wrong economy. It absorbs an impact once, the damage that matters is inside the shell where you cannot see it, and a resale price tells you nothing about whether it has already done its job. Everything else in a loadout can be bought second hand and judged on wear. Storage counts too: a shell left in sunlight or hung on a mirror ages faster than the date stamp inside it suggests.

pages.title: Market
pages.purpose: Second hand motorcycles, used parts and pre owned tools sold by their owners, not by Frontier Moto.
pages.lede: Every listing here is second hand and sold by its owner. Condition is stated before price, known faults are listed, and anything only seen rather than inspected is marked as such.

pages.title: Field Notes
pages.purpose: Dated observations, route reports, road conditions, regulations, tests and things Frontier has learned.
pages.lede: Road works, fuel prices, regulation, import duty, and what riders are reporting from routes we have not covered yet.
